beats.en: We measure weight in grams (g) and kilograms (kg). 1 kg = 1,000 g. Small things like a water bottle's contents or a pencil are weighed in grams; big things like a rice bag, a bed or an almirah in kilograms.
beats.speakEn: We measure weight in grams (g) and kilograms (kg). 1 kg  equals  1,000 g. Small things like a water bottle's contents or a pencil are weighed in grams; big things like a rice bag, a bed or an almirah in kilograms.

textbookBox.concept: To read a weighing scale, first look at what one small mark stands for. If 1 kg is divided into 4 parts, each mark is 250 g. If it has 2 parts, each mark is 500 g.

beats.en: To read a weighing scale, first look at what one small mark stands for. If 1 kg is divided into 4 parts, each mark is 250 g. If it has 2 parts, each mark is 500 g.
beats.speakEn: To read a weighing scale, first look at what one small mark stands for. If 1 kg is divided into 4 parts, each mark is 250 g. If it has 2 parts, each mark is 500 g.

beats.en: Two scales may show the same bag differently: one in kg and another in g. A bag of 2 kg shows 2,000 g on the other scale. A double number line helps: every kg step on top matches 1,000 g below, so we multiply by 1,000.

textbookBox.concept: To change kg and g to grams: 3 kg 500 g = 3,000 g + 500 g = 3,500 g. Shrenu's kitchen scale shows only grams, so for 2 kg 250 g of flour it must show 2,250 g.
